title: Policy: publishable post-incident summaries (scope, timing, approvals, Dedicated/Private handling)
creator: Paula Mendes
description:
Goal
Define Redwood’s policy for customer-facing post-incident summaries: what we publish, when we publish it, who approves it, and how we handle Dedicated/Private incidents without leaking sensitive customer or capacity details.

Why
Customers are repeatedly asking for consistent, publishable, timely post-incident summaries (impact + mitigation + prevention) and our current practice is inconsistent by team/on-call. Support tickets also indicate confusion when the status page is “green” but a specific capability/region had impact.

Scope
- Public post-incident summary requirements for incidents that appear on the public status page (Hosted API + relevant shared control-plane components).
- Policy for Dedicated/Private incidents (public vs customer-only visibility and wording).
- Timing expectations by severity and what constitutes “good enough” to publish quickly.
- Approval chain and decision rights (IC vs Comms Lead vs Support vs Legal/Security).
- Confidentiality rules and redaction guidelines.

Non-goals
- Rewriting the incident response process end-to-end (see incident roles/RACI ticket + runbook).
- Defining the status page component taxonomy (handled in taxonomy + mapping work).
- Defining internal postmortem standards (this is public-facing summary only).

Deliverable
A written policy that Support/CS, SRE, and Product can point to; used for training Comms Leads and as the baseline for ENG-4823 auto-generation workflow.

Links
- Confluence template (draft): sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/post-incident-summary-template.json
- Incident comms templates: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/incident-communication-templates.json
- Escalation playbook (status disputes): sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/status-page-customer-escalation-playbook.json
- Console linking spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/status-page-transparency-console-integration-spec.json

Policy (final)
1) What gets a public post-incident summary
A publishable post-incident summary MUST be posted for:
- Sev0 and Sev1 incidents that were posted to the public status page.
- Any incident with material customer impact lasting > 15 minutes affecting a public status page component (even if severity is ultimately Sev2).

A summary SHOULD be posted for:
- Customer-visible degradations with notable performance/availability impact, even if mitigated quickly, when Support/CS indicates meaningful customer confusion or escalations.

A summary MAY be posted for:
- Brief (< 15 min) spikes if they triggered a public status incident and the customer experience was noticeable.

2) Timing expectations (publish fast, refine later)
- Sev0: Initial publishable summary within 3 business days of incident resolution.
- Sev1: Initial publishable summary within 5 business days of incident resolution.
- Sev2 (posted publicly): Summary within 7 business days.

If the root cause is still under investigation by these timelines:
- Publish a “preliminary summary” that includes confirmed impact + mitigations + follow-ups underway.
- Add a note: “Root cause analysis is ongoing; we will update this summary when concluded.”
- Update the public summary when the investigation finishes (target: within 10 business days for Sev0/Sev1).

3) Required content (minimum publishable bar)
Each public post-incident summary MUST include:
- Title: capability + region + date (avoid internal service names).
- Customer impact: what users experienced (errors, timeouts, elevated latency, streaming disconnects), which components/regions were affected, and approximate time window.
- Measurable impact: use ranges or high-level metrics when safe (e.g., “elevated 5xx error rates” / “p95 latency increased”). Avoid customer-specific figures.
- Timeline: UTC timestamps for investigation start, mitigation start, mitigation complete, resolved.
- Root cause class: a safe category (e.g., “capacity saturation,” “dependency degradation,” “configuration regression,” “software bug,” “network issue”). Include specific root cause only if it does not reveal sensitive infra/security details.
- Mitigations: what we did to restore service (e.g., traffic shifting, fallback models, rollback, scaling).
- Prevention: concrete follow-ups (alerts, safeguards, tests, capacity, tooling changes). Link to public-facing improvements if applicable.

4) Explicit exclusions (do not publish)
A public summary MUST NOT include:
- Customer-identifying details (names, tenants, account IDs), or any phrasing that implies a specific customer was impacted.
- Exact capacity numbers, GPU fleet counts, region-by-region reserved headroom, or details that could expose our ability to serve demand.
- Security-sensitive details (keys, auth flows, internal network topology, exploitation vectors).
- Vendor blame language; keep neutral and factual.
- Internal service names or incident channel links (use component/capability terms aligned with taxonomy).

5) Approval chain and roles
- Draft owner: Comms Lead for the incident (or delegate assigned by IC).
- Required reviewers for Sev0/Sev1:
  - Incident Commander (accuracy + scope)
  - Support/CS approver (Dev Patel or delegate) for customer impact phrasing + expected questions
- Conditional reviewers:
  - Legal (Michael Grant) if the summary includes regulatory/contractual risk language, customer commitments, or could be construed as admitting breach.
  - Security/Compliance (Naomi Feldman) if any incident involves auth, access controls, suspected abuse, or data handling concerns.

Approval rules
- Default: IC + Support approver sign off before posting Sev0/Sev1 summary.
- If IC is unavailable within 1 business day of draft readiness: SRE delivery lead (Rafael Mendes) may approve in their place.
- If Support approver is unavailable: CS leadership delegate (Jasmine Liu or Rachel Kim) may approve.
- Legal/Security are “blockers” only when explicitly invoked by IC/Support approver or when the incident category is security-sensitive.

6) Dedicated and Private incidents
Definitions
- Dedicated: customer has reserved capacity; may share some control-plane and common components.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed environment; public status page visibility may be limited.

Policy
A) Dedicated incidents
- If the incident impacts a public/shared component (e.g., Hosted API gateway, shared control plane, shared auth, shared status page components) and it is posted publicly, it follows the standard public summary policy.
- If the incident affects only a single customer’s dedicated cluster or isolated capacity pool (no shared component impact):
  - Do NOT post a public status incident or summary by default.
  - Provide a customer-only summary via Support/CS within the same timing expectations (Sev0: 3bd, Sev1: 5bd) using the same template but delivered privately.
  - If multiple Dedicated customers in the same region/plane are impacted (pattern suggests shared underlying cause) and the impact is customer-visible:
    - SRE + Support + PM on-call decide whether to post a public incident for the “Dedicated Control Plane (Region)” component (or equivalent) without naming customers.

B) Private incidents (VPC/on-prem)
- Do NOT post public incidents/summaries for customer-isolated Private environments by default.
- Provide customer-only summary through the assigned Support/CS channel.
- If there is a Redwood-operated shared service used by Private customers (e.g., licensing/updates, or optional control-plane connectivity) and multiple customers are impacted, we may post a public incident for that shared service component, but keep wording generic.

Standard wording guidance for Dedicated/Private
- Prefer: “Some customers on Dedicated capacity in us-east experienced…”
- Avoid: “Customer X / a large enterprise customer / a specific tenant…”

7) Storage and linking
- Public post-incident summaries live on the public status page incident record.
- Console linking:
  - Hosted/Dedicated shared incidents: Console may link to the public status page incident + summary.
  - Customer-isolated Dedicated/Private incidents: Console may show “Incident details available via your support channel” (no public link), unless explicitly approved.

8) Quality bar & iteration
- “Publishable quickly” is more important than “perfectly complete.” We will publish a preliminary summary and update it later.
- Weekly status accuracy audit findings that point to mismatch between incident scope and status components should feed into improved summary guidance (add an ‘accuracy correction’ note if needed).

Acceptance criteria
- Policy written and signed off by SRE sponsor (Sean Gallagher), Support leadership (Dev Patel), and Legal/Security reviewers for the rule set above.
- Policy language is incorporated into the Confluence post-incident summary template guidance.
- Incident-bot automation ticket (ENG-4823) references this policy for required fields and reviewer routing.
- Support macros/playbook align with Dedicated/Private handling.

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Do we require root cause for publish?
  A: No. Publish preliminary summary without final root cause if needed; include root cause class only.
- Q: Are we committing to customer notification SLAs?
  A: No. These are targets, not SLAs; avoid “guarantee” language.

Risks
- Over-sharing sensitive details under time pressure → mitigated by explicit exclusions + conditional Legal/Security review.
- Blocking on approvals slows publishing → mitigated by defined delegates and preliminary summary allowance.

Rollout
- Train Comms Leads and ICs on this policy in the same enablement session as the new incident templates.
- Update Support/CS playbook and macros to reference policy language for Dedicated/Private.
comments: 2025-11-13 (Paula Mendes): Pulled together initial policy draft based on customer feedback from Support tickets (embeddings/streaming not reflected). Need to lock Dedicated/Private guidance—docs team asked what we can say publicly without implying single-customer issues.

2025-11-14 (Dev Patel): Support request: include a clear section on when we *do not* post public incidents (single-tenant Dedicated issues) and ensure the policy explicitly provides a customer-only summary timeline; otherwise we’ll keep getting “status page was green” disputes.

2025-11-15 (Kira Thompson): Dedicated/Private language needs to avoid suggesting shared infrastructure details (e.g., ‘capacity pool exhausted’ can be too revealing). Recommend using “resource saturation” / “capacity constraints” and keeping it high-level. Also confirm Console shouldn’t link to customer-isolated incidents.

2025-11-18 (Michael Grant): Legal review: OK with timing targets as long as we do not call them SLAs. Add clause: publish preliminary summary if RCA ongoing. Avoid ‘breach’ terminology; use ‘impact’ and ‘degradation.’

2025-11-19 (Naomi Feldman): Security review: add explicit call-out that any auth/access/security-related incident requires Security review before publishing details. Good with ‘root cause class’ approach; avoid specifics that could aid exploitation.
2025-11-21 (Sean Gallagher): SRE signoff with minor tweaks: make IC the required reviewer for Sev0/Sev1; add fallback approver if IC unavailable; emphasize ‘publish fast then update.’
2025-11-25 (Talia Benson): Incorporated all signoff changes. Marking done once Confluence template references are updated and ENG-4823 is linked to required fields + reviewer routing.

2025-12-03 (Talia Benson): Closed loop: Confluence template updated to reflect exclusions + approval chain; ENG-4823 updated to reference this policy for field requirements and reviewer routing; Support macro update tracked in INT-10430.
